_meta.title: AI agent governance under the Amazon Associates Agent Terms
_meta.headline: The Program Policies now contain a dedicated Agent Terms section that directly regulates autonomous software interacting with Program Content. This platform is built to satisfy it.
_meta.definition: "Agent" means any software or service that takes autonomous or semi-autonomous action on behalf of, or at the instruction of, any person or entity.
_meta.cite: Associates Program Policies — Associates Program IP License and Usage Requirements, Section 4 (Agent Terms), updated April 14, 2026

table.caption: Agent Terms, clause by clause, against this platform

rows.requirement: No Agent may access, use or interact with Program Content unless it identifies itself and operates in strict accordance with Section 3 of the Agent Terms; and not at all if Amazon has asked that Agent to refrain.
rows.impl: Every outbound request carries a named identity. The intake client reads a `refrain` list from config and hard-stops on a match before opening a socket.

rows.requirement: Amazon may, at its sole discretion, limit whether and how any Agent accesses Program Content, including by technical measures.
rows.impl: Rate-limit and throttle handling is treated as authoritative: a 403/429 terminates the run with a recorded reason instead of a retry storm.

rows.requirement: In all HTTP/HTTPS requests, identify that the request is from an Agent and disclose the Agent's name by including "Agent/[agent name]" in the User-Agent string (Amazon's example: Agent/AmazonAgent).
rows.impl: User-Agent is fixed to `Zone3AffiliatePlatform/1.0 (Agent/Zone3ProductResearch)` and asserted by a unit test; requests fail closed if the header is absent.

rows.requirement: Do not conceal or obfuscate that access/use/interaction is from an Agent — including by mimicking the speed or pattern of human keystrokes or page navigation, or by completing or circumventing CAPTCHAs or other human-verification measures.
rows.impl: No browser automation, no input humanisation, no CAPTCHA solver dependency in the lockfile. The agent only makes discrete API-style HTTP requests with a declared identity.

rows.requirement: Respond truthfully to any question or prompt seeking to determine whether interactions are coming from a human or a computer.
rows.impl: The declared identity is the answer; there is no fallback UA pool and no residential-proxy layer that could imply a human.

rows.requirement: Do not circumvent or otherwise avoid any measure intended to block, limit, modify or control whether and how Agents access or interact with Program Content.
rows.impl: A block is a result, not an obstacle. Detection of a block sets the field to blank + Unverified and raises a flag for human review — which is precisely how the 3 product rows ended up blank here.

rows.requirement: Caching, timestamping, payload-size and rate rules that apply to Program Content an Agent retrieves.
rows.impl: No image storage; 24h TTL on other content; 40960-byte request cap; ASINs exempt from the storage limit.

rows.requirement: Whatever the Agent publishes, the associate disclosure must remain clear and prominent.
rows.impl: Disclosure is injected by the renderer, not the model — a generated page cannot omit it. `verify_site.py` fails the build on any page missing it.

model_rules.caption: Rules governing the language model specifically

rows.rule: The model may only restate content present in the retrieved evidence pack; any assertion outside it is dropped, not softened.
rows.why: Participation Requirements 2(b) bans inaccurate, overbroad or misleading claims about a Product; fluency is not a defence.

rows.rule: The model never writes Amazon customer reviews, and never paraphrases one.
rows.why: Community Guidelines incorporated by the Agreement prohibit reviews created or edited in exchange for compensation; Part. Req. 5(t) also bars reuse of review content.

rows.rule: The model may not invent a numeric value (price, rating, count, rate) when the field is missing; it must emit a blank and raise a flag.
rows.why: This is the operating rule that produced every blank cell on this site.

rows.rule: No distillation of Program Content into model weights; no reverse engineering of the API.
rows.why: IP License 2(g) forbids deriving underlying components such as a model, parameters or weights, and bypassing security.

rows.rule: Agent actions on Program Content are logged with request identity, timestamp and outcome, retained for the compliance-certificate window.
rows.why: Amazon may request written certification of compliance on demand; IP License 2(h) also requires furnishing a copy of a client application within 3 business days of request.

rows.rule: Autonomous publishing is capped: the agent drafts, the gate blocks, and only rows that pass grounding publish without a human.
rows.why: A material breach permanently forfeits commission income, so unreviewed autonomy over public claims is the largest single risk in the design.
